title: tc-ai-summary
description:
An AI summary of a set of sources – a thread, a meeting, documents, a ticket's history – with a TL;DR, key points
citing their sources, open questions, a note when the sources have moved on, feedback, Copy and Regenerate.

subject.description: What was summarised, named before the counts: "#launch-q3"

sources.description: The sources summarised, in citation order – a point's chip shows its source's number in this list

tldr.description: The one-line gist, shown first and emphasised

summary.description: The summary; may grow while "summarising". Blank lines split paragraphs

points.description: The key points, each with the sources it comes from

length.description: Short or detailed. Changed by the user unless a tc-length-change listener calls preventDefault()

model.description: The model that wrote it, e.g. "Claude Sonnet"

generatedAt.description: When it was generated, epoch ms

now.description: "Now" for the relative time and freshness, epoch ms; unset, the element keeps its own clock

stale.description: The sources have moved on since the summary: true, or how many new items there are. Sources dated after `generatedAt` count too

staleLabel.description: The banner's words in place of "3 new messages since this summary"

feedback.description: Whether it helped: "up", "down" or null. Changed by the user unless a tc-feedback listener calls preventDefault()

sourcesOpen.description: The list of sources under the footer is open

locale.description: The language for dates and numbers, e.g. "en-GB"; by default the browser's

label.description: How the source is named in chips and the list: "Priya in #launch", "Pricing brief.docx"

href.description: Where the source opens; makes its chips and its row in the list links

at.description: When it was written or last changed, epoch ms

AiSummaryPoint.description: A key point, with the ids of the sources it comes from
